job.title: 3D Print Optimization Engineer - June 2027 New Grads
job.descriptionText:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

The Print Optimization Team takes on the challenge of optimizing the intersection of hardware, software, and materials to deliver industry leading print performance. We strive to make our SLA & SLS product line print parts as quickly, reliably, easily, accurately, and beautifully as possible. We are a collaborative team, with a diverse background, passionate about pushing the boundaries of print performance across our product lines.

As a 3D Print Optimization Engineer you will be continuously using your problem solving skills to drive improved performance.

We are customer focused, and the first step of tackling the problem is understanding what the performance boost we are trying to achieve, and how many customers will benefit. Will customers be able to print parts faster? More reliability? Will they be easier to post-process, or print more accurately?

If you’re excited about process optimization, solving multi-disciplinary challenges, and bringing to market the best print performance possible, we want you as a 3D Print Optimization Engineer!

The Job:

- Push the capabilities of our SLA & SLS 3D printing platforms
- Drive root cause analysis, considering mechanics, fluid dynamics, software, chemistry, optics, electronics, thermodynamics, and customer behavior
- Design efficient experiments that tease out underlying behavior in a complicated system of variables
- Tackle multi-disciplinary problems
- Develop and commercialize solutions that make a real and immediate impact on customer print performance

You:

- Are focused on the customer
- Have a strong sense of ownership with great attention to detail
- Are hands-on and willing to cross discipline boundaries to solve a problem
- Work autonomously and learn new skills to tackle objective
- B.S., M.S., or PhD in any science/engineering discipline (all are welcome)

Bonus:

- Coding experience, ideally python
- Experienced in computer-aided design (CAD)
- Understand material properties and characterization
- Participated in the release of a new product

Our Perks & Benefits:

- Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
- Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
- 401K matching and access to financial advisors
- Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
- Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)
- Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it
- Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
- Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats
- Regular sponsored professional development opportunities
- Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
- And of course… unlimited 3D prints

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply.  Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

Compensation:

Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.

Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

The annual base pay range for this role is:
$85,000—$132,000 USD

We are looking for New College Graduates to join our GPU compute architecture and performance engineering team, dedicated to pre-silicon modeling, data-supported architecture exploration, and GPU microarchitecture improvement for LLM inference, agentic AI, and other generative AI workloads. As a Deep Learning Performance Architect, you will help improve the efficiency and scalability of large language models (LLMs), agentic AI systems, and other generative AI models on NVIDIA platforms. You will gain hands-on experience with pre-silicon performance modeling, correlation, bottleneck analysis, GPU architecture studies, and system-level analysis, while collaborating with engineers across kernel, hardware, and performance teams.

This role offers an opportunity to contribute to real-world studies that help shape the performance of next-generation LLMs, agentic AI systems, and other generative AI models in data center and edge environments. You will help develop the system-level modeling and correlation solutions needed for accurate projections and for guiding performance and efficiency improvements in the agentic era.

What you’ll be doing:

- Build or improve pre-silicon performance and system-level models to better understand workload behavior, architecture tradeoffs, and projection accuracy
- Develop correlation methodologies to compare model projections with lower-level analyses or available reference data and improve model fidelity
- Study how GPU microarchitecture and system-level design choices affect end-to-end performance, efficiency, scalability, and projection fidelity
- Identify performance bottlenecks across model execution, kernels, data movement, and system behavior
- Explore and evaluate architecture ideas that improve performance, efficiency, or model fidelity
- Collaborate with kernel, hardware, and framework teams to better understand end-to-end behavior for LLMs, agentic AI systems, and other generative AI models
- Use profiling and benchmarking tools as needed to support model development, analysis, and correlation
- Present findings and insights through clear analysis and visualization

What we need to see:

job.descriptionText:
Company Description

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join Harvard Business School?

Harvard Business School, located on a 40-acre campus in Boston, was founded in 1908 as part of Harvard University. It is among the world's most trusted sources of management education and thought leadership. For more than a century, the School's faculty has combined a passion for teaching with rigorous research conducted alongside practitioners at world-leading organizations to educate leaders who make a difference in the world. Through a dynamic ecosystem of research, learning, and entrepreneurship that includes MBA, Doctoral, Executive Education, and Online programs, as well as numerous initiatives, centers, institutes, and labs, Harvard Business School fosters bold new ideas and collaborative learning networks that shape the future of business.

Job Description

Harvard Business School (HBS) is seeking multiple Predoctoral Research Associates starting in Summer 2027 to support an assigned faculty member in one of the following academic units.

- Accounting & Management
- Business, Government and the International Economy
- Entrepreneurial Management
- Finance
- General Management
- Marketing
- Negotiation Organizations & Markets
- Organizational Behavior
- Strategy
- Technology and Operations Management

Research subjects can include but are not limited to: labor economics, marketing economics, private equity / venture capital disclosures and taxation, decision making and gender stereotypes in shaping beliefs, industrial organization and the market design of digital platforms, media economics and economics of digital platforms, emerging financial technologies and alternative data, political economy and empirical corporate finance, R&D strategy and the economics of innovation, entrepreneurial management, corporate social responsibilities focused on climate change and gender diversity, asset pricing shaping politics and markets, specialized knowledge commercialization and micro-geographic environments shaping innovation, behavioral economics, intergroup inequity, and tech strategy.

Please note the faculty currently hiring include:

- Ray Kluender: Professor Kluender researches analyzes the determinants of financial well-being and the nature of financial distress, traces the frontier of how entrepreneurship and technology can solve social problems, and identifies market failures and the implications for appropriate corrective policies. Current projects involve partnerships with large-scale financial technology companies and employ a wide range of empirical approaches. His predoc researcher will get hands-on experience with every stage of the research project from conception through publication and will develop a wide range of empirical skills to prepare them for PhD programs. A two-year commitment is expected. Professor Kluender's three prior predocs are currently pursuing PhDs at Princeton, Berkeley, and Harvard.
- Maren Hoff
- Christopher Stanton: Conduct empirical and theoretical research in organizational economics, focusing on how markets and workplaces shape competition, productivity, and economic opportunity.
- Zoe Cullen: Professor Cullen is a labor economist whose research examines how information, technology, and firm behavior shape the well-being of workers and society. Her current projects study how artificial intelligence is reshaping the value of human expertise and the distribution of wages across workers and firms, as well as contemporaneous forces determining worker bargaining power. These projects involve large-scale field experiments and partnerships with technology and payroll companies, drawing on administrative data and a wide range of empirical methods. Her predoc researcher will get hands-on experience with every stage of the research process, from designing experiments through analysis and publication, and will build the empirical and institutional skills needed for a top PhD program. Professor Cullen's prior predocs are currently pursuing PhDs at MIT, Princeton, Chicago, and Yale.

Overview: The Predoctoral Research Associate position reports directly to faculty supervisors and administrative manager in the Research Staff Services office.  Ideal candidates will be comfortable in an environment that requires a high level of independence, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to use discretionary judgment.

Primary duties:

- Work under the general direction of HBS faculty on topics central to HBS research agenda.  Provide subject-area knowledge, analysis and interpretation to faculty member.  Identify and explore a wide-range of questions related to faculty’s research agenda.
- Write cases, case supplements, project reports, and policy memos from start to finish creating original writing based on subject-area expertise, research, and interviews, and write articles for applicable business audiences such as Harvard Business Review.
- Develop, design, conduct, analyze, and implement research using data science knowledge and prior knowledge of requested statistical packages. Perform statistical programming. Experience with NLP.
- Manage and manipulate data using requested packages, such as STATA, Python, R, or MATLAB.
- Ensure compliance with department, University, and federal regulations. Complete work with only general direction.  Be aware of department, School, University policies and potential outside research policies.
- Under general direction of faculty member, must be able to take complex research ideas, concepts, and methodologies and apply them to new projects and situations.  Must be able to structure assignments and keep faculty member informed as necessary, using own judgment.
- Build trust and collaboration by being present on-site and engaging directly with colleagues and various constituents.
- Responsible for other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree with a GPA above 3.5 is required.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

Proven evidence of independent research in specific advanced field of study. Evidence of prior high-quality, original academic writing, and background in analysis and interpretation of relevant data, research, news, and literature is helpful. Ability to read academic, subject-specific information and write a reasoned and thoughtful analysis, as well as produce a creative interpretation, is a must.

The candidate must have extremely high standards in terms of quality of work, attention to detail, strong organization skills, and absolute commitment to task completion. Must be able to balance multiple tasks and shifting priorities under tight deadlines at an accelerated pace when necessary. It is helpful if the candidate is familiar with navigating a complex organization, such as Harvard Business School.

Additional Information

- Appointment End Date: This position is approved for a 1-year term (with possibility of renewal/extension). These are term appointments starting summer 2027 through June 30, 2028, with an expectation of reappointment until June 30, 2028, based on funding and performance. All Predoctoral Research Associate roles at HBS are structured as one-year term appointments, but faculty strongly prefer candidates willing to commit for two years.
- Standard Hours/Schedule: 40 hours per week
- Compensation Range/Rate (including Shift Differential if applicable):
- Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
- Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education
- Other Information:

  The recruiting process starts now and continues into 2027 with offers typically finalized in the late spring. The recruiting process is rolling. Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Candidates with external deadlines should notify the recruiter as soon as possible.

  This is a hybrid position which we consider to be a combination of remote and onsite work at our Boston, MA based campus. HBS expects all staff to be onsite a minimum of 3 days per week and departments provide onsite coverage Monday – Friday. Specific hours and days onsite will be determined by business needs and are subject to change with appropriate advanced notice.

  We may conduct candidate interviews virtually (phone and/or via Zoom) and/or in-person for this role.

  A cover letter is required to be considered for this opportunity. All candidates will be expected to submit a writing sample, transcript, and a code sample to be reviewed by an HBS statistician. Harvard Business School will not offer visa sponsorship for this opportunity.

This is a fully remote position from New York, however, the position requires regular travel throughout Nassau and Suffolk Counties (Long Island) for meetings, outreach activities, and in-person events, typically 1–2 times per week, with occasional evening or weekend events. Team members will also be expected to attend quarterly in-person team meetings in New York City. Individuals may also utilize ICF’s Midtown Manhattan office for work if desired.
